$$
\int 2^{x^{3} + 1} x^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "9c3d97b0-c388-5846-b671-21162ba60fb3" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=x^{3} + 1$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(3 x^{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int 2^{x^{3} + 1} x^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{3}\left(\int 2^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int 2^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u=\frac{2^{u}}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\int 2^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{2^{u}}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{2^{x^{3} + 1}}{3 \ln{\left(2 \right)}}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "9c3d97b0-c388-5846-b671-21162ba60fb3" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "9c3d97b0-c388-5846-b671-21162ba60fb3" :question/answer-fields
